a.text: I can have a reason to repair a friendship even when I would rather avoid the awkward conversation. To me, the source is its place in a flourishing life.

b.text: I do not see a universal list of projects that automatically makes a life meaningful. For me, meaning comes entirely from the person investing their care or choices in something.

a.text: I can have a reason to repair a friendship even when I would rather avoid the awkward conversation. To me, the source is its place in a flourishing life.

b.text: I think a life gets all its meaning from the commitments and interests of the person living it. Nothing becomes meaningful for me independently of what I care about or choose.

a.text: My afternoon disappeared into sorting old postcards and finding somewhere to put them. There were enough duplicates to fill a small box, and I kept stopping to read the backs. I see aesthetic quality as something an object has independently of any audience reaction. Now the desk is clear, but the floor has become a temporary storage area, which is probably how this started last time.

b.text: The sculptor has not put one object beside another, but I still think there are two there. Sharing every bit of space does not erase the distinction between artwork and lump.

b.text: My little projects matter because I make them part of what I care about. I think that personal attachment or choice is the whole source of meaning, however impressive the project looks.
